summary: Evaluate the owner idea of tags + grouping (earlier tags as group headings for later rolls) against the real P1 tables

analyses.verdict: The owner's idea works, and most of it is already built. The geography chain in foundation.yaml groups its rows exactly this way: `requires any_of` palette kinds on 56 of the 60 lifelines, 8 of 40 ruins, 9 of 40 contests and 9 of 50 traits; `olgu_families` on the ruin rows; `families` on the tensions; the role `hint`s; the action `fits` matrix. design_arbiter.py filters on these before the die is thrown, which is why the landform, lifeline and action chain never contradicts itself. The contradictions the audit found all sit on edges that have no heading at all. Those edges are trope↔dials, trope↔contest, trope↔lifeline, trope↔spine, trope↔ruin, and one dial↔ruin edge (magic high vs age of mages). The trope break is the one roll in P1 with no key. It has no `requires`, only 2 rows have `conflicts_with`, and its `tags` field (polity, society, ...) is read by no script. The idea has to be built as membership tags (each row lists every heading it fits or refuses), not as physical sections. The palette is a set of 4-12 kinds, most keyed rows fit several headings, and the clash topics run across the parent tables' families. Measured over 3000 seeds, a small set of claim tags (topic: value) removes every modelled clash with no empty pool. The rate falls from 5.7% (the audit pairs) or 7.2% (the extended set) to 0%, and the smallest pool stays 19 rows or more. The rule that must not be taken literally is "every roll drawn only from inside its heading" applied to the current soft weights: several groups collapse to 0-1 rows and variety dies. So the tags should be hard where they state a contradiction and stay soft weights where they only express affinity. No complete rewrite is needed. What is missing is a claim vocabulary, one generic clash check in the arbiter, and a key for the trope, which could be keyed on the dials alone if it moves ahead of the foundation.

findings.title: Group key per P1 roll (the nearest parent that matters)
findings.detail: P0 dials: the root. The owner may set them, so they are never re-keyed and every child adapts to them. Step 1: spine <- {magic, era} (magic is a hard requirement; era is only a weight today). Palette <- spine (`forces`/`forces_one_of`, a fixed lookup), magic (fantastic cap) and era (forces underground). Ruin <- the palette set (membership) plus a MISSING magic claim. Lifeline <- the palette set (membership). Contest <- the palette set plus the lifeline (weights), with rulers/nobility/deep/war claims MISSING. Break target <- the pieces that exist. Action <- target piece x lifeline family / remnant kind / key kind (`fits`). Scars <- action (`bars_scars_on_target`) plus the magic cap. Time: no key. Winner <- the contest roles and the action. Escalation and layout are deterministic. Step 2: trope <- today nothing (only family, by header). Its smallest real key is the dials (era, magic) if it moves ahead of the foundation. Otherwise it needs a union of claims from up to four parents. Tie: no key (4 rows). Lineage <- palette, lifeline and ruin (soft). Traits <- palette (hard), break time (`after_the_break`) and magic. Attitude: no key. Institution role <- contest roles with a hint. Form <- the role's hint (keep it soft). Practice <- lifeline, ruin and scar (soft), plus trope claims later. Sign <- scale. Power: no key. Phenomenon rule <- the ruin's `olgu_families`, or `scar_magic_rule_changed` -> born_of_break. Limit <- palette. User <- time. Question <- contest family. Secret <- the break, plus exclusion of anything the foundation already shows. Villain <- the secret's chooser (the chooser-tie equivalence) plus a question pole. Names <- people, contest and institution.

findings.title: Physical sections do not fit this data; membership tags do (and already exist)
findings.detail: The palette is a set, so a child keyed on it draws from the union of its headings. Physical sections would need an extra die to choose which kind is 'the' heading, and would copy most rows into several sections. Taking the lifeline under single palette-kind headings: 38 of the 56 keyed rows fit 2 or more headings (1.79 memberships per keyed row), 13 of 22 headings hold fewer than 5 rows of their own, and the 8 fantastic kinds hold 0 (only the 4 universal treaty rows). Today's union pool is a median of 39 rows and a minimum of 11. The physical groups that exist today are the families (spine 6x5, ruin 8x5, contest 8x5, lifeline 7x8-9, rule 8x5, practice 8x5, trope 6 families of 3-8). They serve variety (family_wait, families_distinct), not dependency, with one exception: the phenomenon rule's families are the heading, and each ruin row lists the 2-3 it fits.
findings.evidence: Static count (scratchpad groups.py): lifeline headings by own rows, smallest first: volcanic 1, island 1, lake 2, steppe 4, marsh 4, underground 5 ... mountain 15; fits-count histogram {1:18, 2:32, 3:6, all:4}. Ruin: 32 of 40 fit every kind. Contest: 31 of 40. Traits: 41 of 50.

findings.title: The clash topics run across parent families, so family-level headings cannot catch them
findings.detail: 'Hereditary rule' rows sit in three contest families (two_hands, kin, race) and in lifeline/treaty. 'Nobility present' rows sit in three contest families. 'Lived underground' rows sit in 5 families across 3 tables plus the era dial. Only a per-row tag (topic: value) captures these. Seen from the trope side, break_underground_forbidden has four parents (spine, lifeline, contest, the era dial). The rulers tropes clash with contest and lifeline rows. break_iron_is_sacred clashes with lifeline rows. break_no_writing, break_moon_trades and break_night_is_safe clash with the era dial only. break_world_is_young clashes with ruin rows (extended set).

findings.title: The trope break is the one unkeyed roll; its trope-trope clashes are covered only by a family rule that is not enforced
findings.detail: No trope row has `requires`; 2 have `conflicts_with`. The 33 `tags` are topic labels, not claims, have spelling drift (people/peoples, creature/creatures) and are never read. The governance family (7 rows: lottery, guilds, dragons, magic_is_nobility and three more) is the physical group that keeps rulers tropes apart. The header's `families_distinct: true` is only asserted in tests/test_design_tables.py:259, and designer.py preroll_p1 draws `break.{n}` with only `exclude=set(breaks)`. So standard and epic births can draw two governance rows today: about 4.0%, of which about 0.8% are clashing pairs such as lottery+guilds. (This preroll is flagged in its docstring to be replaced by build items 7-10.)

findings.title: Measured: claim tags remove every modelled clash at a small pool cost, in either order
findings.detail: Two orders were modelled with an arbiter-side claims filter. AFTER: the trope keyed on the foundation plus the dials (today's order). FIRST: the trope drawn right after the dials, so it becomes the heading for spine, lifeline, contest and ruin. Both give 0 clashes and 0 empty pools over 3000 births. The keyed side pays in frequency. AFTER (extended set) moves these tropes, per 1000 births: no_kings 46.7->35.3, underground_forbidden 54.3->44.3, no_writing 49.3->39.3, world_is_young 49.7->42.7. FIRST moves contests instead: two_heirs 26.3->22.3, empty_throne 38.0->30.0, sibling_rulers 34.7->29.0. The dial-keyed clashes (writing, sky, magic) cost the same in both orders. FIRST fits the owner's wording ('earlier tags are headings') and the plan's own reason for the trope ('it inverts defaults the later rolls read'). It gives the trope a one-parent key (the dials) and spreads the cost over the 40-60-row foundation tables. It does change the owner-approved order (review #1), and the tie would still be rolled after the foundation.
findings.evidence: Scratchpad claims.py, 3000 seeds, dials drawn with the dials.yaml weights. Core set, ORDER=none: 172 of 3000 births (5.73%) hold a clash (rulers 57, sky 36, writing 35, deep 25, magic_now 8, nobility 7, iron 5). Extended set: 216 (7.20%). AFTER: trope pool min 19, p5 23, median 30. FIRST: contest pool min 24, p5 31; spine min 22; ruin min 30.

findings.title: Turning today's soft weights into hard headings would destroy variety
findings.detail: If 'draw only inside your heading' were applied to the existing weight_by and hint rules: the institution form for the role's hint would have 1 row in the median (fully determined). The spine rows the dials boost would be 0 in 34% of births (medieval, renaissance and ancient boost nothing at standard scale). The lineages a weight favours would be fewer than 5 in 27% of births. The tension group per contest family is 5-11 rows, which is fine. So hard membership should be reserved for contradictions (claims) and for the fits that are already hard (palette kinds, `fits`, olgu). Affinity stays a weight.
findings.evidence: Scratchpad hard.py over the 3000 births. institution_form per hint: criminal, guild and scholarly 1 row each, martial 3, the rest 2. Lineage favoured group: min 1, p5 3, median 6. Spine boosted group: 0 in 34.2% of births.

findings.title: Existing groups under 5 rows, and what cross-birth exclusion does to them
findings.detail: Action per (lifeline, craft) = 4 rows and (remnant, wasteland) = 5, with `row_wait 3` and a target+action pair that never repeats. It is hit in 1.8% of births; the sim's action pool has min 4 and p5 6. Phenomenon rule under scar_magic_rule_changed = born_of_break, 5 rows (3 when time_coming, because two rows are after_the_break). It is hit in 11% of births, and with `avoid_used: true` the group runs dry after about 45 births, after which the usage fallback brings repeats back. The palette's 'a height' and 'a water' draws are 3 rows each, and palettes are never excluded across births, so that is harmless. Time has 4 rows and break_target 5-6 (avoid_used false). The tension groups hidden_hand and two_hands have 5 rows each (soft). No foundation draw fell below 11 rows except those listed.
findings.evidence: Scratchpad act.py and sim.py pool sizes (dN): action min 4 / p5 6 / median 9; sig.rule min 3 / p5 5 / median 10; lifeline min 11; contest min 30; ruin min 33; spine min 24; trope min 25; trait.visible min 14; limit min 11; user min 7.

findings.title: Tags scale better than id lists
findings.detail: The modelled coverage needs 40 claim assignments on 9 topics (extended set), or 40 pairwise conflict entries in `conflicts_with` form. The counts are similar today, but a new row costs one tag instead of an edit to every opposing row, and pairs grow multiplicatively as tables grow. The arbiter needs one generic rule: a row is excluded when a topic it claims already holds a different value, unless the topic declares the two values compatible. Dial values carry claims too (era=underground: deep lived, sky none; era=renaissance: writing print; magic=high: magic plentiful). The existing `requires: {dial: ...}` machinery can already express those.
findings.evidence: Scratchpad count.py. Only 4 conflicts_with lines exist today across foundation.yaml (1), trope-breaks.yaml (2) and tensions.yaml (1).

risks: The modelled claims are my reading of the audit pairs plus a few additions (more nobility contests, mass war, a young world against the old_peoples ruins). A real vocabulary needs the owner's row-by-row review, and contradictions hidden in sub-row text (for example contest escalation lines such as 'iç savaş' or 'haritaların çalınması') are only caught when the row as a whole is tagged.

Over-tagging turns affinity into law. Each hard tag lowers the tagged rows' frequency (break_no_kings_only_guilds -35% after the foundation), which works against the owner's wish for variety and multiplies usage fallbacks under used.json.

Moving the trope ahead of the foundation changes an owner-approved order (plan item 25 review #1). The tie still has to come after the foundation, and the trope's inversions of the foundation (lineage homes, weapons) would then have to be honoured by the foundation's draws.

Small groups plus avoid_used or row_wait (born_of_break 3-5 rows, action/craft 4) run dry and fall back to reuse, so repetition returns without anyone seeing it. Every hard group under about 8 rows needs a check on how fast it is used up.

The secret and villain tables could not be modelled here beyond counts (archetype 24 rows, 2 with conflicts; villain_shape 15, 3 forbidden; origin 10, 1 forbidden). Their clash surface against the foundation's claims is unmeasured.
families_distinct for trope breaks is declared but not enforced in designer.py preroll_p1; until build items 7-10 replace it, governance tropes can co-occur.
analyses.recommendation: Implement the owner's idea as membership tags inside the existing arbiter, not as physical sections, and not as a rewrite. (1) Add a `claims: {topic: value}` field to rows and to dial values, plus a small topics file that declares each topic's values and any compatible pairs. Add one generic arbiter check: exclude a row when one of its topics already holds a different value, logged as reason 'claim'. Retire the trope `tags` field or rename its values into claims. (2) Tag hard only what is a literal contradiction: rulers, nobility, iron, deep, sky, writing, magic abundance, mass war, history depth, as a start. Keep every affinity (lineage by palette, form by hint, tension by contest family, era and tone boosts) as weight_by, because hard versions collapse to 0-1 rows. (3) Give the trope a key. The structurally cleaner option is to roll it right after P0, so it is keyed on the dials alone and becomes a heading for spine, lifeline, contest and ruin (cost: contest pool min 24). The option that keeps the approved order is to key it on the claims union (cost: trope pool min 19). The owner should choose, and the tie stays after the foundation in both. (4) Enforce families_distinct in the trope draw. (5) Extend the model-free many-seeds test so it asserts zero claim clashes, reports every group under 5 rows, and reports how many births each small group lasts under avoid_used. Watch born_of_break (3-5 rows) and the action/craft group (4 rows) first.

analyses.verdict: Grouping by earlier tags removes contradictions of one class by construction: a later roll clashing with an earlier roll it can see (a, parent to child). That holds only when each draw is filtered by the tags of every earlier roll, not by one heading. All nine audited contradictions are class (a), because the trope break and the ruin are rolled after the dials and the foundation they clash with. But the trope table's rows clash with five different parent pieces at once: the era dial, the spine or palette, the lifeline, the main contest, and epic's second contest. So one heading per table cannot cover them. In a 3000-seed simulation, the best single heading (the dials) would prevent 94 of 151 clashes (62%), and the contest heading 28 (19%). Grouping the trope table as a tree of heading-to-row-list would need about 295 distinct heading combinations for these nine keys alone. Drawn instead from "rows whose tags fit every tag rolled so far", the owner's grouping becomes exactly the proposed claims check, run by the arbiter, which already filters the pool before the die. Grouping does not solve the other four classes by construction. (b) Siblings: two later rolls that don't see each other, e.g. the lottery trope against the question "inheritance vs merit", or a trope keyed to contest 1 missing contest 2. (c) Two rows from the same table: both draws share the same heading. Today's `families_distinct` flag is read by no script, and cross-family pairs like world_is_young with no_writing slip past it anyway. (d) Later phases: P2 and later prerolls see P1 only through the one pantheon override. (e) Prose: the writer's text and the script's own sentence templates. So the owner's idea works as the authoring model: rows carry tags, and later draws come from the compatible group. But it needs a compatibility check underneath: claims with incompatible values and a scope, applied against all rolled tags, inside the same table, across phases, and at the door. Grouping is not a replacement for that check; the two are one mechanism seen from two sides.

findings.title: All nine audited contradictions are parent-to-child (class a), and grouping prevents each one only if the right key is present
findings.detail: The trope break is step 2's first roll, so it sits after the dials and the whole foundation; the ruin sits after the dials. Key needed per case: (1) lottery vs two_heirs/sibling_rulers: a contest key (succession: hereditary), from contest 1 AND contest 2. (2) no_kings_only_guilds vs two_heirs/empty_throne/lords_peasants/old_order_reform plus life_binding_marriage: nobility: exists, from contest and lifeline (two parents). (3) iron_is_sacred vs life_iron_coal/life_famous_steel: lifeline key (iron: plentiful), one parent. (4) underground_forbidden vs era underground, spine_three_depths/mountain_within, life_deep_lake/deep_mouth/mushroom_fields, contest_surface_deep: four parents, but one palette key (land_underground) covers 97%. (5) magic high vs ruin_age_of_mages: dial magic, one key, on the ruin table. (6) renaissance vs no_writing, (7) underground vs moon_trades, (8) underground vs night_is_safe: dial era, one key each. (9) dragons_rule vs two_heirs: a contest key (ruler: mortal, hereditary). Several single-key cases, but they fall on the same table (the trope), so that table needs every key at once.
findings.evidence: 3000-seed sim (scratchpad/coverage/sim.py): 151 hits. Offending row by parent piece: dial alone 88, spine alone 16, lifeline alone 5, main contest 27, epic's second contest 9, two pieces at once 6. Prevented by a single heading: dials 94/151 (62%), main contest 28 (19%), spine 21, lifeline 6, second contest 9. Only all five together give 151/151.

findings.title: A heading tree is combinatorial; a per-row tag filter is not
findings.detail: Taking 'the earlier tags are the group headings' literally, with each heading owning its own row list, the trope table would need one hand-built group per combination of the keys the clashes turn on. Letting each row carry tags and filtering by compatibility with everything rolled gives the same coverage for 1-3 tags per row. That filter is the claims proposal.
findings.evidence: 295 distinct combinations of (era, magic, underground in palette, relevant lifeline, relevant contest) in 3000 births; the theoretical product is 5x3x2x7x7 = 1470. Filter cost measured: mean trope pool 33 -> 32.05, minimum 26; at least one trope row barred in 1609/3000 births (54%).

findings.title: The gap is authoring, not mechanism: the trope table has no conditions at all
findings.detail: design_arbiter.py already filters the pool before the die against every rolled row (requires any_of/all_of/none_of, dial, symmetric conflicts_with). The lifeline already works the owner's way: it is grouped by palette tags. The trope table is where 8 of the 9 audited clashes land, and it has zero requires and zero weight_by. What's missing is a vocabulary: today a clash has to name every row id. no_kings would need 5 ids, underground_forbidden 7, and each new row breaks the list. The trope `tags` field (polity, society...) holds topics, not claims.
findings.evidence: cond.py counts. lifeline: 56/60 rows require palette kinds. contest: 9/40 require, 30 weight_by. ruin_source: 8/40 require. trope-breaks.yaml: 33 rows, 0 requires, 0 weight_by, own conflicts on 2 rows. tensions.yaml: 0 requires (family weight x3 only). magic.yaml#regulator: 9 rows, 0 requires, 0 conflicts.

findings.title: (b) Siblings are not solved by grouping each table under its own parent
findings.detail: The question's home is the contest (tensions.yaml header, family weight x3). The contest two_hands (e.g. contest_one_harbour) fits both the lottery trope and tension_inheritance_merit, so neither heading sees the other; only the explicit conflicts_with stops the pair. Likewise, a trope keyed to the main contest misses epic's second contest.

findings.title: (c) Same-table pairs: grouping gives nothing; the family flag is unenforced and too coarse
findings.detail: Two draws from one table share the same heading. trope-breaks.yaml declares `families_distinct: true`, but no script reads it. designer.py preroll_p1 draws break.2 with exclude=set(breaks) only. Enforcing the family flag stops the governance clashes, but not cross-family ones such as world_is_young ('written history is three hundred years old') with no_writing ('writing is unknown'). Epic's second contest only needs another family, so two succession contests can meet.

Cross-family world_is_young+no_writing: 2/1977. Two of two_heirs/empty_throne/sibling_rulers in one epic birth: 4/3000.

findings.title: (d) Cross-phase: later prerolls do not see P1 tags, except one override
findings.detail: preroll_p2 (designer.py ~319-327) is the only live case of 'an earlier tag decides the next roll': a trope's overrides.pantheon_type forces the pantheon. Everything else in P2 rolls freely. break_magic_is_nobility's P2 hook says 'magic's regulator is the nobility itself', yet magic.yaml#regulator is drawn from 9 rows with no condition; at most regulator_crown_office fits. Headings also flow only forward: break_moon_trades carries overrides.era_bias (trope-breaks.yaml line 201), which no script reads. The era is rolled in P0, so a later row cannot steer it; the clash has to be a condition on the trope instead.

findings.title: (e) Prose-level clashes are outside grouping; the script's own templates are one source
findings.detail: sentence() in design_foundation.py prints contest role texts verbatim, and s2 always opens with 'Çok önce'. 11 of 40 contest rows print ruler, noble or kingdom nouns into the sentence (the audit named 5). The world_is_young trope ('no ancient secrets') meets an old-age ruin source. Grouping cannot reach the writer or the templates. Claims can feed the door's word patterns (rows-doc section 13 #8). The kingdom texts also show why claims need a scope: contest_foreign_envoy's kingdom is abroad and should not trip a local nobility: none.

risks: A partition (each heading owns its own row list) would multiply authoring about 295-fold for the trope table alone. Small groups would also empty the pool: the arbiter raises EmptyPool and stops the birth when the constraints leave no row.

Smaller groups exhaust avoid_used faster. The trope table never repeats a row another campaign drew, so a small group drops into usage_fallback, which repeats rows. That is the cross-birth repetition the owner dislikes.

Positive membership ('this row fits heading X') fails safe but costs variety. Negative claims ('clashes with Y') keep variety, but a forgotten tag lets a clash through. Either way the many-seeds test must assert zero clashing claim pairs.
Tags without scope over-exclude: 'a distant kingdom's envoy' should not trip a local nobility: none.
Headings flow only forward. Whichever of two clashing tables is rolled later must carry the key; an earlier table cannot be steered (the dead era_bias override).
The nine audited pairs are a sample. Contest role texts, the 'Çok önce' template and world_is_young show more, so the 3.5-5% rate is a floor.
The prose (writer and templates) and P2+ prerolls stay exposed unless the same claims reach the door and the later prerolls.
analyses.recommendation: Adopt the owner's idea as the authoring model, but build it as one mechanism with two faces. Every row gets tags, and every draw is filtered by compatibility with all tags rolled so far, not by a single heading. Implement this in design_arbiter.py as claims: topic and value, incompatible values declared per topic, a scope (local or abroad). Keep today's families, requires and weight_by for thematic fit. Order of work: (1) Tag the dials and the trope table first; the trope table has no conditions today and takes 8 of the 9 audited clashes. Put the underground claim on the palette kind land_underground, which covers 97% of that case. (2) Tag the foundation rows the trope clashes with: the contests' ruler, nobility and succession claims, including their role texts, and the lifelines' material claims. (3) Enforce families_distinct, which no script reads today, and apply claims inside a table for the second trope and epic's second contest. (4) Pass the same claims into the P2+ prerolls, starting with magic.yaml#regulator against break_magic_is_nobility, and to the door's word patterns for the prose. (5) Extend the model-free many-seeds test to assert zero clashing claim pairs over all rolled rows. analyses.verdict: From the variety side, the owner's "tags + grouping" idea is workable if a group means "every row that does not contradict what is already rolled" (membership by exclusion: a row is in unless a claim rules it out). It is costly if a group means "only the rows listed under the earlier roll's heading" (membership by inclusion: a row is out unless listed). I measured both on the committed tables with the real arbiter and foundation roller, plus a model of step 2, over 2,000 single births and 40 sequences of 40 births with used.json simulated. Exclusion-style tags (the audit's claims) cut births with a literal clash from 5.0% to 0.35%. They cost about 0.8 of the 33 trope-break rows (effective pool 27.3 to 26.5) and 0.1 bits out of about 153 per birth, so variety is practically unchanged. Hard inclusion groups at the density the owner's own affinity lists already have (a row listed under about a quarter of the headings: tensions 0.235, olgu 0.263) cut the per-table effective pools by 4 to 7 times: trope break 27.7 to 6.9, question 28.6 to 7.5, institution form 12.6 to 1.8, lineage 13.5 to 4.1. They make 4% of births hit an empty pool. Among campaigns with the same contest family, the share that draw the same trope break rises from 7% to 26%. They also fix only the clashes whose partner is that one heading. 57% of clash occurrences are against the era dial, 20% the contest, 11% the spine, 8% the lifeline and 5% the ruin against the magic dial. Intersecting four headings to cover them all leaves 2.3 effective rows and empties the pool in 22.5% of births. Recommendation: use tags to exclude everywhere, and use hard inclusion groups only under specific, many-valued headings whose groups hold at least about 10 rows (these exist already and work). Use soft weights (×2-3) for theme under the few-valued headings (dials, families, role hints). Before any grouping, fix two usage-rule faults that already produce repeats.

analyses.recommendation:
Take tags and grouping in their exclusion form. Every row carries a few claims (topic: value, e.g. nobility: none; iron: rare; below_ground: forbidden; writing: absent). The dials carry claims too (era underground: sky none; era renaissance: writing printed; magic high: magic plentiful). The next roll's group is every row whose claims fit what is already rolled. This removes about 93% of clash births for about 3% of trope rows and 0.1 bits per birth.

Keep hard inclusion groups only where the heading is a specific row from a large table that rotates by itself and the group keeps at least about 10 rows after the other filters: phenomenon rule ← ruin olgu_families, action ← target fits, lifeline ← palette kinds. All three exist and measure well.

Use soft weights (×2-3) for theme under few-valued headings: question ← contest family (tensions family_weight 3 as planned), institution form ← role hint (hint_weight 3), lineage ← palette and lifeline, and, if wanted, trope break ← contest or ruin. Do not make these hard: they would drop to 7.5, 1.8, 4.1 and 6.9 effective rows. Never intersect several hard headings.

Fix the usage rules first, whatever is chosen:
- In design_foundation.py:166/180, draw actions and scars with avoid=False, or make design_dice.usage honour the header's avoid_used, so they wait 3 births as item 25 says.
- Make the arbiter's fallback graded: drop used_elsewhere but keep row_wait and pair before dropping everything, so 'not in the last 3 births' survives when a table or group runs out.
- Give naming families, trails and other small pools a wait window instead of avoid_used.
- Add to the many-seeds test a group-size floor (every heading × constraint cell has at least N rows) and a repetition check over simulated birth sequences (like exp2) next to the no-conflict proof.

analyses.verdict: Yes, the owner's idea can be built, and it is already how the arbiter works. design_arbiter.arbitrate() narrows the pool to the rows that fit every earlier roll, and only then throws the die. Grouping through earlier rows already exists: 86 `requires: any_of` lists on palette ids decide which lifelines, ruins, contests and traits can come, and the phenomenon rule is filtered in code to the ruin's `olgu_families`. Two things are missing. First, the vocabulary: headings today are only single row ids, and the dial rows are never in the arbiter's Context. Second, the negative side: nothing records that two rows assert opposite facts. The groups cannot be written by hand. In 3,000 simulated births every earlier-roll context was unique (3,000 of 3,000), and even at family level there were 1,977 distinct contexts out of 5,040 possible. So a "heading" has to be worked out at draw time, as the overlap of what each earlier row's tags allow. That is exactly the arbiter's filter. With tags on rows, the idea is a small extension, not a rewrite. I built a model-free prototype that stores tag tokens in the Context and derives conflicts from them, with no change to arbitrate(). It used 7 topics and 26 tag holders. It removed every audited pair: 0 of 3,000 births, against 4.90% before, and 0 of 2,250 across all 45 scale × magic × era combinations. It caused no empty pools, and the trope-break table's variety was essentially unchanged: entropy went from 5.040 to 5.036 bits, where 5.044 is the maximum for 33 rows. The one caveat: tags only guarantee compatibility for what is tagged. The system enforces the registry; it cannot make the registry complete.

What cannot be expressed today: (a) a heading made of an earlier row's family (for example 'the lifeline is a craft'), (b) a dial row as a heading for `conflicts_with`, and (c) 'these two rows assert opposite facts' without listing every pair by hand.

Two ways of building the Context: token expansion placed only in add() would silently skip design_dice.context (P2+ from disk) and every test built with Context(rolled=...).

Secret layer: tokens set by secret or villain rows that constrain later public draws (P2+) hide the reason (the existing routing), but the smaller pool and die size can still hint at them. Tokens need their secret flag carried, and their exclusions must be counted, never named.
Forced rows (spine forces, forces_by_dial, implies, adds_palette) that clash with a dial's claims turn into a runtime EmptyPool through check_forced unless a static test catches them first.
A new table or topic that forgets its claims: without a per-table review stamp, adding a topic never forces the older tables to be re-read.

Review load for the owner: the plan requires every conflict and requirement list to be shown to the owner like the rows. The registry and per-row claims are more compact than pairs, but they still need approval (secret and villain claims as counts only).
analyses.recommendation: Build the owner's idea as tags on rows, with the arbiter working out each heading's group before the die, as one small build item before item 10 (the identity roller). Do not restructure the tables into per-heading sub-tables. (1) Add a closed registry of topics in data/design, each topic with its values, whether it is exclusive or which values clash, and its scope. Add a test that every row's `claims` uses registered values. Drop or convert the unused trope `tags`. (2) Change design_tables: add claims_index(), add automatic family tokens, and merge the derived clashes into the cached symmetric index. Change design_arbiter.Context: seed the dial row ids and their tokens in __post_init__, and expand tokens in add() and for a `rolled=` passed at construction. Make conflicting_pairs expand tokens as well. Leave arbitrate() unchanged. (3) Use three kinds of relation, matching the plan's own words. 'Needs' becomes a hard group, as requires any_of on tokens, and only where the row cannot exist without the earlier fact. 'Clashes' is derived from the claims and is the default. 'Fits better' stays weight_by on tokens. (4) Migrate in this order. Dial rows and the audited rows come first, because seeding the dial ids alone clears 62% of the hits. Then the 10 time_coming guards, the craft and dragon lists, and trope-breaks, followed by tensions and the signatures. The development tab tags secrets and antagonists and shows the owner counts only. (5) Tests: registry closure; symmetric derived clashes; identical tokens on both ways of building a Context; the many-seeds test extended to the identity once item 10 lands, with the audited pairs pinned; no EmptyPool across the 45 dial combinations and a pool floor per draw; a static check that forced rows never clash; row reachability plus entropy and frequency floors per table; secret-token routing; and a `claims_reviewed` stamp in each P1 table's roll header that fails when a topic is added, so no table silently forgets its tags. The owner should hear that tags remove the contradictions the registry names, and that completeness comes from reviewing each topic against each table.

design_rules: R1 (the owner's rule, made exact): every draw is thrown on the group of rows that are compatible with everything already rolled: the dials, every earlier row of every table, the earlier draw of the same table, and earlier phases. The group is computed by the arbiter at draw time. It is never written out as a physical sub-table, and it is never one heading alone.

R2 (three kinds of tag, three strengths, matching the plan's own words). (a) `claims: {topic: value}` is a fact the row asserts about the world. It is HARD and works by exclusion: a row leaves the group when one of its claims clashes with a claim already rolled. This is the default tool for consistency. (b) `requires: {any_of: [claim:topic=value | row id]}` means 'needs': the row cannot exist without the earlier fact. It is HARD and works by inclusion. It is allowed only when the heading is a specific row of a large table that rotates by itself and the group keeps about 10 rows or more (median) after the other filters. (c) `weight_by` on a tag means 'fits better': SOFT, x2-3. Every theme link under a few-valued heading (dial values, families, role hints) stays soft.

R3 (what earns a claim): a claim is written only where two rows' sentences contradict literally. This is the owner's conflict principle of 2026-09-29. A reading that makes a story is no clash, and affinity is never a claim. Candidates such as world_is_young x an old-age ruin (65 of 3,000 births) go to the owner under this principle; they are not tagged automatically.

R4 (closed registry): one new data file, e.g. data/design/claims.yaml, lists each topic, its values and which values clash. The default is that two different values of one topic clash; the registry may declare compatible pairs. A test checks that every row's claims use registered topics and values, as ecology_tags are checked today. The unread trope-break `tags` field is dropped or converted into claims. It has 19 values, two spelling drifts (people/peoples, creature/creatures) and no reader.

R5 (starter vocabulary, for the owner's review): rule (hereditary / lottery / guild_council / dragons / mages), nobility (exists / none), iron (plentiful / sacred_rare), below_ground (lived / forbidden), sky (open / none), writing (printed / absent), magic_now (plentiful / faded), mass_war (exists / ritual_only). This is about 9 topics and about 40 claim assignments. Modelled over 3,000 seeds, it clears all nine audited pairs.

R6 (the dials are the root and carry claims): examples are era_underground {sky: none, below_ground: lived}, era_renaissance {writing: printed} and magic_high {magic_now: plentiful}. The owner may set the dials, so they are never re-keyed; every later roll yields to them. The dial rows' ids and their claims are placed in the arbiter's Context. Today only the dial values are kept there, so a clash naming a dial row never fires.

R7 (claim at the highest common ancestor): put `below_ground: lived` on the palette kind land_underground. That one tag covers 97% of the underground case (641 of 660 births). Only the few rows that assert the fact on other ground carry it themselves, e.g. life_deep_lake on a desert.

R8 (scope by not claiming): a claim is a world-wide fact of the home land. A row whose fact belongs to a foreign land (contest_foreign_envoy's kingdom) or to one region carries no claim on that topic, or a narrower value. No scope machinery is added unless the owner's review finds a case that needs it.

R9 (mechanism, the only new code): claims become tokens `claim:topic=value` in Context.rolled, and every rolled row also adds `family:<table>=<family>`. design_tables derives the clashes from the registry and merges them into the symmetric conflict index it already caches. requires, none_of, weight_by and conflicts_with then work on tokens unchanged. arbitrate() does not change. conflicting_pairs expands tokens, so the door's recheck and the many-seeds test see claim clashes. Both ways of building a Context expand tokens the same way: the in-memory add(), and design_dice.context, which builds from disk. A token set by a secret row keeps the secret flag, and its exclusions are counted, never named.

R10 (inside one table): the second trope break and epic's second contest see the first draw's claims. families_distinct is enforced by the roller. It is declared today but read by no script, and about 4.0% of standard or epic births currently draw two governance tropes.

R11 (implicit tags become real tags): the ten `none_of: [time_coming]` guards next to `after_the_break: true` become a claim on the break's time. The craft-lifeline id list (written twice) becomes `family:lifeline=craft`. The two different dragon lists (5 and 8 ids) become one claim. A new row then joins a group by carrying one tag, instead of someone editing every opposing row.

R12 (floors): a hard group that can fall under 5 rows fails the build test. A group under 8 rows gets a run-out report from a simulated sequence of births under used.json. Two hard few-valued headings are never intersected: four of them leave 2.3 effective rows and empty 22.5% of pools.

R13 (usage rules, because groups make pools smaller): the arbiter's fallback becomes graded. It drops used_elsewhere first and keeps row_wait and pair; only then does it drop everything. Today it drops them all at once (design_arbiter.py line 173). design_dice.usage honours a header's avoid_used: false. Today actions and scars are drawn with avoid=True by default (design_foundation.py lines 166 and 180), so they are excluded for good instead of for 3 births. Small pools such as naming families (10 rows, used up by birth 4) get a wait window instead of avoid_used.

R14 (completeness is a review, not a mechanism): each P1 table's roll header carries a `claims_reviewed` stamp listing the registry topics it was read against. Adding a topic fails the test until every table has been re-read. The owner reviews the topic list and the per-row claims the same way as rows, with full lists. Claims on the secret and villain rows are tagged by the development tab and shown to the owner as counts only.

R15 (order): keep the approved P1 order. The trope break stays step 2's first roll, and its group is the rows compatible with the dials and the whole foundation (pool minimum 19, median about 30 of 33). Trope-first (right after P0, becoming a heading for the spine, lifeline, contest and ruin) also measures 0 clashes, with a contest pool minimum of 24. That option is an owner decision, because it reverses review #1, and the tie would still be rolled after the foundation.

R16 (beyond P1): the P2+ prerolls build their Context with the same tokens, starting with magic.yaml#regulator against break_magic_is_nobility. The same claims feed the door's word patterns, so the prose and the script's sentence templates are held to them too.
grouping_solves: Parent-to-child contradictions, which is the class of all nine audited pairs (8 land on the trope table, 1 on the ruin table). This works when the group is 'compatible with every earlier tag'. Result: 4.9-5.7% of births (7.2% on the extended set) fall to 0 over 3,000 seeds and all 45 dial combinations, with no empty pool.

Sibling clashes, once the check runs against everything rolled rather than one parent heading. Example: the lottery trope, then the inheritance-vs-merit question, a pair a contest-family heading would miss (2 of 3,000 births without the hand-written conflict).

Same-table second draws (the second trope, epic's second contest), because the second draw sees the first draw's claims. An example is world_is_young with no_writing across families (2 of 1,977 births).

Replacing hand-copied id lists with one tag each (time_coming x10, craft x2, dragons in two versions). A new row joins its group by carrying a tag, not by edits to every opposing row. The pairwise review matrix is 139,369 cross-table pairs against about 545 per-row claim decisions.

Thematic fit where the heading is a specific row of a large rotating table, which is already working: lifeline by palette kinds (effective pool 37.8, never fell back in 40 births), phenomenon rule by the ruin's olgu families (first repeat around birth 33-35), action by target fits (9.0 effective rows).
grouping_does_not_solve: One heading per roll cannot guarantee compatibility. The trope clashes with five parents at once (dials 62%, main contest 19%, spine 14%, second contest 6%, lifeline 4%). A heading tree would need about 295 hand-built combinations for that one table, and intersecting four hard headings empties 22.5% of pools.

Untagged facts. The system enforces the registry; it cannot make the registry complete. 0% on the audited pairs is not 0% contradictions. For example, 11 of 40 contest role texts print ruler, noble or kingdom nouns, and world_is_young meets an old-age ruin in 65 of 3,000 births. Completeness comes from reviewing each topic against each table (R14).

Steering an earlier roll from a later one. Headings flow forward only: the era is rolled in P0, so break_moon_trades' `era_bias` override can never act, and the later table always yields. Tagged trope rows lose 15-25% of their frequency, e.g. underground_forbidden 159 to 127 per 3,000 births.
Prose: the writer's text and the script's own templates (sentence() prints contest role texts verbatim, and s2 always opens with 'Çok önce'). These need the same claims at the door's word patterns.

Repetition. Small hard groups under avoid_used run dry, and the arbiter's all-at-once fallback then brings back the previous birth's row. Grouping makes this worse unless the usage rules are fixed (R13). Today scars already run out by birth 11, with 20.5% near-repeats.
Distinctness rules. families_distinct, forces and forces_one_of concern difference between draws, not compatibility, so the roller must enforce them. families_distinct is unread today.
Later phases, unless the P2+ prerolls build the same Context with tokens (design_dice.context from disk). Today only the pantheon override crosses from P1 to P2.
Soft weights never guarantee consistency: at x3 on the same links, the clash rate stays at 5.0%. Weights carry theme only.

synthesis.variety_cost:
In its exclusion form the idea is nearly free.

What claims cost:
- Trope-break effective pool: 27.3 to 26.5 rows (-3%).
- Information per birth: about 0.1 bit lost out of about 153 bits (152.9 to 152.8).
- Trope entropy: 5.040 to 5.036 bits, against a maximum of 5.044.
- Trope pool: minimum 19, median about 30 of 33 (with the trope rolled after the foundation).
- Only the tagged rows lose frequency, and only in births where they would clash: underground_forbidden 159 to 127 per 3,000 births, no_kings 46.7 to 35.3 per 1,000, no_writing about -20%.
- Trope-first would move that cost onto the contests instead (two_heirs 26.3 to 22.3 per 1,000; contest pool minimum 24).

The inclusion form is costly when every theme link becomes hard:
- Effective pools shrink 4-7x: trope 27.7 to 6.9 rows, question 28.6 to 7.5, institution form 12.6 to 1.8, lineage 13.5 to 4.1.
- 4% of births hit an empty pool.
- 26% of campaigns with the same contest family share a trope break, against 7% today.
- The first cross-birth fallback comes at birth 12 instead of 20.
- Intersecting four hard headings leaves 2.3 rows and empties 22.5% of pools.

So hard inclusion stays only where it already measures well (lifeline, phenomenon rule, action), and theme stays soft. The existing usage faults cost more variety today than claims would: scars are used up by birth 11 and naming families by birth 4. The usage fixes (R13) are part of the recommendation.
risks_and_mitigations: Completeness illusion: a fact nobody tagged still passes. Mitigation: the `claims_reviewed` stamp per table (adding a topic fails the test until every table is re-read); the owner reviews topics and claims like rows; the many-seeds test asserts zero claim clashes and pins the audited pairs.

Over-tagging turns affinity into law, and variety and cross-birth freshness fall. Mitigation: R3 (a claim only where the sentences contradict literally); R2 (theme stays weight_by); pool floors and frequency floors per table in the many-seeds test.

Topics too coarse or too broad create false clashes that shrink the late tables. Example: a foreign kingdom's envoy tripping 'nobility: none'. Mitigation: R8 (a foreign or regional fact carries no claim, or a narrower value); values stay specific; the registry can declare compatible pairs.

Small hard groups plus avoid_used or row_wait run dry, and the all-at-once fallback returns last birth's rows unseen. Mitigation: R12 floors; graded fallback and honouring avoid_used: false (R13); a run-out report for groups under 8 rows. born_of_break (3-5 rows) and action/craft (4 rows) are watched first.

Two ways of building the Context: token expansion placed only in add() would silently skip design_dice.context and the twelve test sites that pass rolled=. Mitigation: expand in __post_init__ as well, plus a test that both paths give identical tokens.

Secret leakage through tokens: a claim set by a secret row shrinks a public pool, and the die size could hint at it. Mitigation: the token keeps the secret flag (Context.add already ORs it); its exclusions are routed to the secret side and counted, never named; the development tab tags the secret and villain rows, and the owner sees counts only.

Forced rows (spine forces, forces_by_dial, adds_palette) that clash with a dial's claim become a runtime EmptyPool through check_forced. Mitigation: a static test that no forced row can clash with any dial value's claims.

Order bias: the later table always yields, so tagged trope rows become rarer. Mitigation: accept it, since the dials are the owner's; or the owner chooses trope-first, which moves the cost to the 40-row contest table; frequency floors in the test.

The measurements rest on analysts' models of step 2 (items 8-10 are not coded) and on their reading of the audit pairs. Mitigation: re-run the many-seeds and birth-sequence simulations on the real roller once item 10 lands; the audited 3.5-5.7% rate is a floor, not the full count.

Owner review load: the plan requires every condition list to be shown like rows. Mitigation: one short topic list plus about 40-120 per-row claims is far smaller than pair lists, and it is reviewed once per topic per table.
synthesis.migration:
The owner asked to agree the system first and to talk about applying it to the build items after that. So this is an outline, not a schedule. Each step is one green commit.

- Step 0: the owner approves the topic list and values (R5), the three strengths (R2) and the order decision (R15). This is plain Turkish, full lists.
- Step 1, independent of tags: the usage fixes. Graded fallback in design_arbiter; design_dice.usage honours avoid_used: false; actions and scars wait 3 births; naming families get a wait window. Tests pin the repeat rates.
- Step 2, the machinery (a new build item placed before item 10, the identity roller, because that roller is not coded yet): the claims registry file and its closure test. In design_tables: claims_index(), family tokens, and derived clashes merged into the cached conflict index. In design_arbiter.Context: seed the dial row ids and their tokens, and expand tokens in add() and __post_init__. conflicting_pairs expands tokens. The new data file joins PLANNED in test_design_tables.py. About 70 lines and 8-10 tests; arbitrate() and the Roller are unchanged.
- Step 3, data: tag the dial values, land_underground and the audited rows (trope about 10, lifeline about 6, contest about 11, ruin 1). Convert the implicit tags (the ten time_coming guards, the craft list, the dragon lists). Drop or convert the trope `tags` field. Assert zero claim clashes over thousands of seeds and across all 45 dial combinations, with no EmptyPool.
- Step 4: build item 10 on tokens. It enforces families_distinct, uses the olgu group, keeps hint and family weights soft, and applies claims to tensions and the new signature sub-tables. The development tab tags secrets and antagonists and reports counts only.
- Step 5: the claims_reviewed stamp in each P1 roll header, pool floors and run-out reports in the many-seeds test, and a static forced-row check.
- Step 6: the P2+ prerolls use the same Context (regulator first), and the claims feed the door's word patterns.

No test birth runs in the development tab. The new birth, run by the owner in the Opus tab, comes after P0 and P1 are complete, as the plan already says.

It rejects the owner's literal reading with a strawman ('rows would be copied'), although per-row membership lists would need no copying. holes.claim_attacked: R9 / R14 / risks #6: a token set by a secret row keeps the secret flag; its exclusions go to the secret side and are 'counted, never named'. R16: P2+ prerolls use the same Context.
holes.failure: arb.pick writes notation d{len(pool)} and raw = the pick's position in the filtered pool to the PUBLIC record. Any secret-driven shrink therefore shows as a smaller die than the public exclusions explain, and raw narrows down which rows went. A single secret claim reaches every tagged row in every later public table (all of P2+ under R16), so the public dice log reads out the secret's claims. Context.add ORs the flag, so a token set by both a public and a secret row becomes secret: exclusions a public row fully explains disappear from the public log, and that disappearance shows the secret shares the claim. The owner also reviews the full registry (R4/R14), so any topic or value added for secret rows is visible to them, and 'counts only' still leaks the theme spread.
holes.example: scratchpad/leak.py uses the real arbitrate() on pantheon.yaml#type (5 rows), with one secret-flagged token clashing with dead_gods and silent_gods. The public record shows excluded: [], {notation: 'd3', raw: 2, row_id: 'pantheon_dualist'}. The owner sees 5 rows, no public exclusion and a d3: two rows were removed by the secret layer. From the raw position and the table order they can narrow down which two.

holes.claim_attacked: Order: 'headings flow forward only' (grouping_does_not_solve #3); R15 'keep the approved order'.
holes.failure: In the code, a rerun's Context holds every OTHER phase's latest attempt, later ones included. design_dice.prior_rolls() skips only skip_phase. dm.stale() only relabels later phases and leaves their dice_log and dm-only records in place. So a P1 rerun (or revise --reseed) made after P2-P4 were prerolled is filtered by P2-P4 rows. Once claims exist, these backward headings are broad: stale later rows shrink P1 pools, can empty them (EmptyPool stops the rerun), and P4's secret rolls (faction.N.secret, secret=True) shape public P1 draws, with the die-size leak above. The proposal's claim that 'today only the pantheon override crosses from P1 to P2' is also wrong: the cross-phase plumbing already exists. The gap is data (no P2+ row references a P1 row).
holes.example: Roller.__init__ calls dd.context(campaign, skip_phase=phase), which calls prior_rolls(): it takes every record whose attempt is its phase's latest, for every phase except the one being rerun. design_manifest.stale (lines 491-505) sets status only. A P1 rerun at the P4 review therefore runs with P2-P4 rows, secret ones included, in its Context.

Applied consistently under R3 + R16, every P2 calendar moon row presupposes a sky (even moon_none_stars, 'only stars'), so P2 hits EmptyPool in every underground birth (about 11%). Not claiming leaves the clash in place; claiming makes false clashes. The per_roll_keys give people traits no rule claims.

holes.failure: There is a whole class of presuppositions: a row names an antecedent that was never rolled. It is not a clash between two rolled rows, so no topic review finds it. It is exactly what the owner's positive grouping catches, and the proposal drops that part.

holes.failure: The cost is measured on single births and a 40-claim vocabulary. First, across births the trope table (33 rows, avoid_used, no row_wait) runs out by itself, and R13's graded fallback gives it no floor, so last birth's trope can return. Second, completing the registry (holes 1-2, which R14 requires) puts dial-level claims on the root, and those remove late-table rows for every birth with that dial value. holes.claim_attacked: R14 claims_reviewed stamp; R9 tokens in ctx.rolled; risks #7 (the static forced-row test covers dial claims).
holes.failure:
Four maintenance gaps:
- The stamp is per table, so a row added to a stamped table passes with no review.
- Tokens share ctx.rolled with row ids, so every consumer that treats it as row ids (tests' rolled(), the door, cards) now sees tokens.
- family:<table>=<fam> tokens are outside the closed registry, so a misspelled family never fires and nothing reports it.
- The forced-row check covers dial claims only, but under R16 later forced rows (P4 quota archetypes, P3 settlement kinds, the pantheon override) meet claims from rolled P1 rows. check_forced then raises a runtime SystemExit mid-preroll.

critique.verdict:
The plumbing is sound and worth keeping: turning claims into tokens the arbiter already understands, arbitrate() unchanged, enforcing families_distinct, and the usage fixes. The proposal as written is not ready to adopt. It overstates what it guarantees: 'compatibility guaranteed' is really 'no clash among the pairs it tagged'. Against the real tables and code it lets through clash classes that together are more frequent than the audited 3.5%:
- unaudited literal pairs, such as war_is_ritual with the war dial (2.7%) and mining or envoy rows beside the forbidden-descent and forbidden-border tropes;
- promise-level clashes in hooks, dial effects, scale parameters and forced quotas: at least one in 17.6% of births (magic_is_nobility against every magic dial's regulator, no_kings against P4's forced state faction, world_is_young against the epic scale's 500-year history);
- presuppositions (the departed god's temples with no departed god; the break's orphans and wound under a break still coming);
- scope clashes between people traits and land-wide rule.

For the promise-level class, exclusion is the wrong tool: it makes the trope yield to the defaults it exists to invert. The proposal has no 'overrides' relation.

Two starter claims are wrong:
- sky: none on the underground era contradicts the owner's ruling that the surface is rare, not gone. Applied consistently, it empties P2's moon table in every underground birth.
- below_ground on land_underground makes false clashes under the proposal's own principle. It halves the forbidden-descent trope (144 to 73 per 3,000 births), while the proposal quotes -20%, the cost of a different rule.

Secrecy is not solved. The public die size and the pick's position show secret-driven exclusions: demonstrated as a d3 with no public exclusion on a 5-row table. The OR'ed token flag and the owner-reviewed registry leak as well.

The rerun path already feeds later and secret phases into an earlier phase's Context, so headings do not flow forward only.

Adopt the tokens, but only after fixing the items below. Then re-measure with the real identity roller and a completed vocabulary, and show the owner the availability cost for each trope row.

Scratch scripts: C:\Users\armag\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-armag-Desktop-Campaign-Designer\8d6f4f98-10d0-4c4d-9722-45585aa189da\scratchpad\ (sim.py, sim2.py, sim3.py, ug.py, seq.py, leak.py, xref.py).
must_fix_before_adopting: Add an 'overrides' relation (a trope rewrites a dial effect, a scale parameter, a forced quota or a later hook) for clashes between a trope and a default, instead of excluding the trope. Otherwise show the owner, per row, how often each trope becomes unavailable (magic_is_nobility, no_kings, war_is_ritual, dungeons_inhabited, world_is_young).

Build a secret firewall. Public draws must never be filtered or weighted by tokens from secret rows, or the public notation and raw must be computed on a public-only pool. Keep per-token provenance instead of Context.add's OR'ed flag. Keep secret-only topics and values out of the owner-reviewed registry, and per-topic counts off public surfaces.

Fix design_dice.prior_rolls so that a phase's Context holds only earlier phases, by phase order, with no stale or later phase and no later secret records. Do this before claims widen backward headings.

Drop sky: none from era_underground, or take it to the owner together with its consequence: P2's calendar moon table runs empty in every underground birth. Move below_ground claims off the land_underground landform and onto rows where people live or work below, and add the mining rows (contest_mine_owners_miners, iron_coal, copper_mine, gemstones).

Registry semantics: no default clash between the values of a topic. Declare clashes explicitly, or support implication (printed implies written; a magic nobility is hereditary). Add a scope for each claim (land, people, region, foreign polity), and do not convert theme lists (dragons, craft) into hard claims.

Widen the completeness review: hooks and dial effects, not only row statements, plus a presupposition pass (a row naming 'the X' must require X, or the break-has-happened claim). Stamp each row by a content hash rather than each table.
Settle whether the new-taboo prohibition draw is the first or the second trope. Then give that group a floor or a wait window: R12 as written fails on it.

Restate the figures honestly: '0 contradictions' means 0 among tagged pairs; R7's cost is -49%, not -20%. Re-run the many-seeds and birth-sequence measurements on the real identity roller (build item 10) with the completed vocabulary before the owner approves the topic list.
